Subject: Performance impact summary — latency, streaming UX & concurrency (Finly)

Hi Amit,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate the context on the payment-notifications use case. I wanted to capture what I heard (high level), confirm a few numbers, and propose next steps so we don’t lose momentum.

One‑line summary
- Finly needs to support a conversational notifications flow (user asks about transaction status, model streams incremental updates) without degrading UI responsiveness or customer experience. Latency spikes during concurrency peaks are the main blocker for rollout.

What you told us (pain points)
- Sporadic tail latency during peak business hours — some requests exceed 1.5–2s at the token level, causing the UI to appear frozen.
- Streaming UX is degraded: first-token latency is inconsistent and partial renders are arriving in jittered chunks.
- When load ramps (campaigns, payroll runs) concurrency goes up ~5–8x and upstream rate limits/backpressure cause retries and SLO misses.
- Current workaround (shorter prompts + client-side truncation) is brittle and hurts quality.

Current stack (as discussed)
- Backend: GKE + Node microservices.
- Model: mix of OpenAI hosted endpoints and a small self-hosted LLM for embeddings.
- Traffic pattern: steady baseline + scheduled bulk bursts (approx. 700–1,200 concurrent conversational sessions during peak).

Target success criteria (what Finly wants to be able to measure)
- P95 single-turn generation <= 350ms for non-streamed short-completions (90 token median).
- First‑token streaming latency <= 180ms, smooth per‑token delivery after first token.
- Sustained concurrency across the fleet of up to 1,000 concurrent active sessions with graceful degradation (no hard failures).
- End‑to‑end UX: perceived response time under 400ms for interactive flows.

Risks we flagged
- Bursty traffic pattern may require prefix/KV caching and adaptive batching to avoid higher unit costs.
- Quantization/compatibility if you plan to host model variants on-prem later.

Proposed next steps (short)
1) Technical deep‑dive with your infra engineer and our runtime lead — focus: traces, sample tokens, and concurrency profile (30–45m). Marcus to lead ops conversation.
2) Provide a short artifact list: light perf traces, representative prompt set, and a small sample of streaming traces (we asked for this in the call).
3) 2‑week trial PoC: a scoped route with a small subset of users to validate p95 and streaming UX.

Attachments I’ve added to the thread: finly-arch-diagram.png (what I sketched in the call), initial-traces-snip.txt (sample trace excerpt).

Proposed slots for the deep‑dive (all times ET):
- Tue 22 Jun — 10:30–11:15 or 15:00–15:45
- Wed 23 Jun — 09:00–09:45 (preferred for our infra lead)

If those don’t work, tell me a couple of windows and we’ll align.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park

From: Amit Desai <amit@finly.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Finly Engineering <eng@finly.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 23:01:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Performance impact summary — latency, streaming UX & concurrency (Finly)

Kimberly —

Thanks for the write-up, this is accurate and helpful. A few clarifications / extra detail from our side:

- Concurrency: our production telemetry shows typical peak windows reach ~850 concurrent interactive sessions, but during a few internal campaigns we’ve seen short spikes up to ~1,300 sessions for 10–15 minutes. We’d like graceful degradation (serviceable partial responses) rather than hard failures.
- Targets: 350ms p95 is fine as a starting target. For streaming we’d prefer first token <= 150–180ms, after which tokens should stream in reasonably even chunks. If the first token is fast but subsequent tokens come in clumps, UX is still bad.
- Current model path: we push most traffic to OpenAI right now; we have a smaller internal inference pool (NVIDIA T4s) for a separate experimental avatar product.
- Observability: we use DataDog traces + Honeycomb for some async traces. I will attach the OTel span snippet and a small trace file.

We’ll get the artifacts you requested attached. Happy to trial a scoped route — need to align on data retention and encryption (we’re PII-adjacent).

Deep‑dive windows: Wed 23 Jun 09:00 ET works for our infra lead (Ravi). If Marcus can take that slot, great.

Best,
Amit
Amit Desai
Head of Platform Engineering, Finly
amit@finly.com | +1 (212) 555‑0189
